text: Driving into a busy parking lot, you just want to find a spot. You're looking for the quickest, easiest path through the maze of cars.
But notice how strictly everything is laid out: the angled spots, the one-way arrows. It often feels like the lot is forcing your movements.
Why not just straight-on spots or two-way aisles everywhere? It seems like a simpler, more 'efficient' design at first glance, right?
The secret is optimized flow. Angled spots are much easier to enter and exit, preventing backups. One-way aisles eliminate head-on collisions.
This design sacrifices a bit of perceived 'freedom' for significantly higher overall throughput, safety, and a surprising amount of space efficiency.
Next time you park, you won't just see lines. You'll recognize a carefully engineered system guiding every car for everyone's benefit.
